supported_claims: RAGWarrant governance produced a CRAG mock-API governance superiority signal on full held-out validation.
A behaviorally distinct follow-up over sanitized frozen CRAG mock-API observations found governed selection reduced measured cost at equivalent proxy-plus-evidence quality.

The CRAG v1.1 local generative primary slice found reduced measured cost at equivalent generated-answer quality under sanitized metrics, but repeats did not reproduce the cost result; a second pinned local model produced no positive cost-result slices; a faster non-thinking instruct model repaired answer emission; unguarded latency selection was mixed; a label-aware guardrail was inconclusive; a learned deployable quality-risk predictor reduced validation expansions but produced mixed confirmatory latency evidence with two quality-loss slices; guardrail v2 pooled validation across offsets and blocked promotion after held-out quality loss; HotpotQA confirmed a nonconstant quality signal but remained inconclusive.

The open-source/arXiv readiness package supports RAGWarrant as a governance and promotion-control framework with a public mini reproduction, external evaluator input adapters, selector ablation matrix, CRAG evaluator-mapping diagnostics, and sanitized AIM hardware characterization.

The cloud-agnostic deployment-readiness package supports RAGWarrant as a finite open-source governance job with CLI, Docker, Docker Compose, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Azure, AWS, GCP, artifact-sink, and promotion-decision schema assets.
Docker static validation passed and the hardened container runtime smoke-test path completed the public-mini governance job locally.

The RC1 reproducibility package adds fresh-clone reproduction, release-candidate manifests and checksums, verify-run artifact integrity, selector stress testing, external evaluator adapter v2 demos, CRAG evaluator mapping v2 diagnostics, HotpotQA quality-signal audit v2, sanitized AIM hardware matrix, and an arXiv systems/methods scaffold.
The strongest CRAG mock-API decision was decision-reproduced in Docker and replicated under frozen-observation resplits according to packaged artifacts.
RAGBench HotpotQA supports context-retrieval policy variation, not full corpus-backed retrieval.
unsupported_claims: broad generative LLM governance validation beyond the current mixed bounded local CRAG/HotpotQA evidence
key_limitations: Raw licensed datasets are not redistributed.
The behaviorally distinct follow-up is derived from frozen sanitized observations and uses proxy-plus-evidence quality, not human-calibrated or generative validation.

Generative validation synthesis is mixed: the primary CRAG qwen slice showed reduced measured cost at equivalent generated-answer quality, but CRAG stability repeats did not reproduce the cost result, a second pinned local model did not recover it, a faster non-thinking instruct model repaired answer emission, unguarded latency selection was mixed, the label-aware guardrail was inconclusive, the learned deployable risk predictor reduced validation expansions but produced confirmatory quality loss on two slices, guardrail v2 blocked promotion after held-out quality loss, and HotpotQA remained inconclusive.
The readiness synthesis supports open-source and arXiv tooling posture, not a universal governance superiority claim.
Deployment-readiness artifacts are portability templates and local job contracts; live cloud execution is not claimed.
Docker runtime validation completed locally in this session; live cloud execution and production operation remain unclaimed.

Fresh live CRAG now has a restored local mock-API runtime and sanitized live sample, but remains blocked because the sample did not produce a usable answer/evidence quality signal; HotpotQA produced an operational-gain-with-quality-loss result under stronger answer-label/supporting-fact metrics.
RAG Compass ranked fifth in the strongest CRAG mock-API result.
